q: (CH3)2NH is an example of which class of amine?
why: Two hydrogens of NH3 are replaced by methyl groups, giving a secondary amine R-NH-R'.

q: The Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is preferred for preparing amines because it gives
o: A mixture of primary, secondary and tertiary amines
why: Unlike direct ammonolysis of alkyl halides, Gabriel synthesis avoids further alkylation, yielding pure primary amine.

q: Hoffmann bromamide degradation converts an amide R-CONH2 into an amine with
o: One carbon more than the amide
One carbon less than the amide
Two carbons less than the amide
why: The carbonyl carbon is lost as CO2 (via Na2CO3), so the resulting amine has one carbon fewer than the starting amide.

q: In aqueous solution, the basicity order of aliphatic amines is generally
why: A balance of +I effect, steric hindrance and solvation of the cation gives secondary > primary > tertiary in water.

q: Aniline is a weaker base than methylamine mainly because
o: The nitrogen lone pair in aniline is delocalised into the benzene ring
Aniline has a higher molecular mass
Aniline has no lone pair on nitrogen
why: Resonance delocalisation of the lone pair into the ring makes it less available to accept a proton, lowering basicity.

q: In the Hinsberg test, which type of amine does NOT react with benzenesulphonyl chloride at all?
why: Tertiary amines have no N-H to be substituted, so they do not react with Hinsberg's reagent.

q: The product formed by a primary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride is soluble in excess KOH because
o: It still has an acidic N-H that forms a soluble salt with KOH
why: The remaining acidic N-H in the N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide reacts with KOH to form a soluble potassium salt.

q: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test, using CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH, is a positive test specifically for
why: Only primary amines (R-NH2) react with CHCl3/KOH to form foul-smelling isocyanides; secondary and tertiary amines do not react.

q: Diazotisation of aromatic primary amines must be carried out at
why: Diazonium salts are unstable and decompose above 5 degree C, so diazotisation is done at 0-5 degree C.

q: A benzenediazonium salt reacting with phenol in weakly alkaline medium gives
o: A coloured azo dye via coupling
why: Diazonium salts couple with phenols/anilines to form brightly coloured azo compounds without losing nitrogen.
